results.correct_value: The south-slopes approach starts at the Watson Lakes trailhead (~4,000-4,200 ft, end of FR 1107), crosses the ~5,300 ft saddle below Mt. Watson to Diobsud Lakes, continues past Bacon Peak to the Hidden Lake saddle (~4,553-4,560 ft), then bushwhacks north through two cliffbands to Hagan's south benches.
results.evidence: A Bacon-Hagan-Blum trip report starts at the Watson Lakes trailhead (4,200 ft), crosses the 5,300 ft saddle below Mt. Watson to Diobsud Lakes and reaches Hidden Lake (~4,553 ft) at the Bacon-Hagan low point; a Watson-Blum traverse report likewise starts at Watson Lakes (~4,000 ft) and ends at the Baker River trailhead (800 ft); the peak's route page describes the south approach from the Bacon-Hagan saddle bushwhacking north through two cliffbands. No source describes a bushwhack from Sulphide Creek Camp to Hidden Lake — the Baker River trail approach is the NORTHERN (Blum Lakes) line leaving near Blum Creek. The row's approach, descent_text and approach_logistics therefore describe an undocumented line, but a correct rewrite needs the Diobsud-to-Hidden-Lake leg (around/over Bacon Peak, which itinerary day 2 also omits) and the trailhead pin/approach_logistics coordinates sit at the Baker River trailhead (out of scope), so no patch is written; this needs a coordinated rewrite of approach, descent_text, approach_logistics, waypoints[0] (name/elev/coords) and itinerary day 2.

results.correct_value: The standard south-slopes route itself crosses a short section of the Hagan Glacier (around its ice apron) below the summit slabs.
results.evidence: A traverse report describes crossing firm snow around the Hagan Glacier's ice apron with crampons to a dike-notch, then Class 3 to the summit; a second traverse report describes crossing the glacier on the Hagan massif; the peak's route description has parties scrambling slabs to the summit from the glacier. So the route is not non-glaciated and the glacier hazard is not only for parties extending to Blum/Bacon. Whether to rope is left as is (one report found the glacier flat enough to cross without crampons).

results.fact: Which finish is the route: Class 4 summit gully or exposed NW Ridge
results.correct_value: The row mixes two finishes: the common 100-ft Class 4 gully (tops out on the NW summit) and the rarer steep snow to the NW-SE notch then the SE peak's exposed Class 4 NW Ridge (the route's namesake).
results.evidence: The Ruth-Icy Traverse route page describes ~500 ft of 2nd-3rd class to a 100-ft 4th-class gully that can be rappelled or downclimbed; the peak page says most parties climb the NW peak, which holds the register. The one detailed account of the Northwest Ridge line climbed steep snow directly to the NW-SE notch and then the SE peak's steep, loose, wildly exposed NW Ridge with a Class 4 knife-edge, explicitly not the gully. climbing_route steps 5-6 therefore describe the gully route, not the named NW Ridge; rewriting them needs more than one source on the ridge line, so no patch (beta's summit identity is fixed separately).
